title: Historical Value
text: “…Hmm, so you’re one whose whereabouts have been untraceable this whole time. So, what business do you have here?”
“Give me information.”
“Information about what?”
I wanted to say “the Crimson Swine”… but I needed to phrase it in a way the information broker would actually understand.
“The Melromarc princess studying abroad in Faubrey.”
“What, did that woman do something to you too?”
Oi, Crimson Swine. Being famous even in a place like this is really saying something, I say.

“She’s got quite a few people holding grudges against her. If she weren’t the daughter of the Wise King of Wisdom with all those troublesome connections, somebody would’ve assassinated her by now… Honestly, if she’d just kept her head down, none of this would’ve happened.”
Ah, I see. So there was quite the backstory here.
“Well, the King of Faubrey’s got his eye on her too, so she’s fated to disappear eventually. Just wait your turn and be patient.”
Fuhaha, that’s certainly one option, but letting her live is more trouble than it’s worth, so I’ll be swift about it this time, indeed.
“Hmph. Want me to just erase her for you?”
Here, I figured I’d play along with the man’s griping.
“Hah! If you think you can pull that off, go right ahead and try.”
“If you don’t tell anyone later that you got information out of me, I might consider it.”
“If you can manage it, I’ll keep quiet.”
This might be a stroke of luck, I say.
“Talk, and I’ll erase you too… where is she?”
He seemed about to toss back some glib remark, opening his mouth for a second before shutting it again. After a beat, he spoke.
“…You serious?”
“What, scared?”
“Hah! Just telling you her location isn’t scary at all.”

Spit it out already, you coward! These people call themselves assassins for a living and can’t even take down one measly Crimson Swine—pathetic lot. He swept his hand open, demanding payment. Haggling was such a bother. Still, thinking that, I pulled out some valuables I’d confiscated from a griffin’s nest. A worn-out golden crown I recognized from a previous loop. As for coins, I prefer to save those for buying Filolial-sama eggs since they’re easier to use in trade—so I prioritize handing over the harder-to-convert stuff like this to people of this sort.
“What’s this?”
“Figured this’d be worth more to you lot than gold coins. Sell it off for cash.”
I said it in a deliberately suggestive tone, indeed.
“We’re not a pawnshop… where’d you even get something like this?”
“Smashed up some monsters and found it.”
No need to hide it awkwardly, so I just told him straight.
“Dragon treasure or something? Those things hoard all sorts of stuff sometimes… Going by the feel, the weight, the reaction—it does seem to be gold, but…”

The assassin guild’s information broker spent a good while turning the crown over, examining it intently. It was definitely gold, no doubt about that. For the record, my spear’s appraisal showed it was just a crown made of gold with no special effects, studded here and there with gems. A bit of pocket money, I say.
“Tch. Oi, call a merchant.”
And so the assassin guild summoned some merchant they apparently had on retainer. After a while, a merchant came shuffling in.
“Calling someone out at this hour—what is it?”
“Appraise this.”
“What? Oh? This is…”
The merchant’s face turned rather serious as he scrutinized the crown intently.

“A crown of this design—famous for having been specially commissioned around nine hundred years ago by a king, though whether it was Fobla or Nemamuge depends on which history book you check. No special effects, but if it’s genuine, it holds enormous historical value. Apparently it was a ceremonial ritual item used in royal succession back then.”
“Heh.”
Not me, mind you. The information broker gave an uninterested reply.
“Most of these turn out fake, don’t they?”

“Ah, there are an enormous number of forgeries, since genuine ones sell for so much. If it’s the real thing, it’s a museum-grade rarity. The kind of thing wealthy collectors would pay sums rivaling a small nation’s budget to acquire—that’s how coveted it is.”
Which is why there are so many fakes, the merchant continued.

“However, long ago, a wealthy man of the time, drawn by its rarity and value, paid a fortune to purchase it and had seasoned warriors escort it during transport. But monsters—dragons, griffins, that sort—attacked and stole it, and it was lost. A national-scale order of knights hunted down the monsters responsible, but the item was never recovered. To this day it’s said to be held either by some ancient dragon demon lord, the king of griffins, or possibly the Filolial Queen.”

So it was said to be in the possession of a Great Filolial-sama too, apparently. Unfortunately, it seemed she didn’t have it. Though… I’m sure Great Filolial-sama would love this too, given how fondly she carries around sparkly crystals and the like, I say.
“Is there any way to tell a real one apart?”

“Ah, if it’s genuine, there’s an engraving and inscription carved into the underside of this crown. It uses a technique that’s been lost to time now, so it’s easy to spot. Once forgeries get made in excess, appraisal techniques catch up too. So telling real from fake at a glance is… ……………is there one?”
The merchant tilted his head, staring at the mysterious engraving on the underside of the crown.
“I need to go wake up some colleagues. This might be extremely dangerous.”

And with that, moving at a pace somewhere between a full sprint and a walk, the merchant went tearing off. The information broker watched his retreating back intently, then tilted his head while holding the crown I’d brought. About ten minutes later, maybe? Starting with that merchant, several more people connected to the merchants’ guild showed up, taking turns examining the crown, casting appraisal magic over and over as they talked amongst themselves.
“There’s no way this is genuine.”
“But still—”

Among these merchants was one I recognized—someone who’d done business with Father before. Apparently he was a fairly famous merchant even in Zeltoble. Eventually, four out of five raised their hands to say it was genuine. They were probably trying to keep their voices down, but my ears caught every word.
“Oi, where’d you get this, you!”
While I’d been silently watching the proceedings, the merchant apparently finished his discussion and turned to question me.
“Did the appraisal come back yet?”
“Answer my question first.”
“You haven’t explained anything yet, have you?”
I deployed the negotiation tactics passed down directly from Father, I say.
“…It was fake. Not worth much. Honestly, don’t bring junk like this around here.”
“Then give it back, won’t you?”

Father’s voice in my head judged that these merchants were lying, so I reached out to take it back—and the merchants’ faces went panicked. One merchant shot a sharp glance toward the information broker, signaling something, so I immediately grabbed him by the collar and slammed him into the ground.
“You bastard! What are you trying to do!”
“Wha— He took him down that easily!?”
Seemed like there’d been a fairly skilled one mixed in among them.
“You’re the ones who tried something. So the ‘fake’ story was a lie, wasn’t it?”

I made sure to keep up the intimidation so as not to show any openings. What exactly was so special about that crown, anyway? Frankly, if you sold something like that to some random merchant, they’d probably say the design was outdated, pry out the gems, and melt it down for scrap—that’s the kind of item it was. Since having the original owner make a fuss over it later would be a hassle, on Father and the others’ orders, I’d sometimes heat things like this with magic myself and turn them into gold ingots before selling them. I’d seen that happen a few times during the loops.
“Answer me.”
“…Seems this one’s pretty skilled. What do we do?”
“Tch!”
The battle-ready assassin guild members and the merchants clicked their tongues and set the crown down in front of me.
“This is the genuine crown of a legendary fallen nation, one with real historical value. Where did you get this?”
“Found it in a monster’s nest.”

“Don’t joke around. There’s no adventurer in this world who could bring back something of this historical value from a monster’s nest. This is the kind of item said to lie deep within the lairs of those wicked, vicious griffins and dragons—places no mere human could handle!”
“That much was nothing worth mentioning. Then how about this?”
And with that, I casually pulled out a goblet I’d also secured, setting it down beside the crown.
